$data.description: Reusable pull-request facts supplied by a review host.

pull-request.description: One observed pull request, including its Markdown author description, revision, diff statistics, and checks.

guidance.producer:
Replace the complete source whenever the pull request or its checks change:

```bash
leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id> --file pull-request.json
```

The JSON object carries `repository`, positive integer `number`, `title`, `author`, `base`, `head`, `revision`, `status`, a Markdown `description`, RFC 3339 `observedAt`, a complete `diff` object, and a `checks` map from check name to status. Keep the source id on the same pull request for the page's lifetime. Leaf presents these supplied facts; it does not query a forge.

description.description: The author's pull-request description as Markdown. Raw HTML is displayed as text.

lf-pull-request.description: A compact, commentable account of the pull request being reviewed. Author an empty element with an id, and bind its required `request` input through `source`. The widget renders the original author's Markdown description safely and keeps it visibly labeled and separate from the surrounding reviewer's or agent's analysis. Repository identity, revision, branch path, status, diff statistics, observation time, and named checks all come from the typed source.

x-guidance.author: Place one empty `lf-pull-request` before the agent-authored walkthrough and bind it to the page's pull-request source. The widget labels the original author description itself, so the surrounding prose can stay the reviewer's analysis.

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable, unified call-tree diff supplied by an analysis host. Author an empty element with an id, bind its required `document` input through `source`, and point `diff` at the exact `lf-diff` evidence. The widget groups CallDiff's adjacent unchanged, removed, and added tree items under collapsible changed roots instead of redrawing two independently laid-out graphs. Each rendered row is a stable projected datum, so a user can comment on one item or select its exact text; source coordinates navigate to a matching line in the bound patch.

x-guidance.author: Capture authentic CallDiff plain-text output as a `text-document` and bind `lf-call-diff` to it. Keep unchanged tree items in the capture: they are the stable landmarks that make the structural change readable. Prefer one focused file or entry point per widget for a large repository. Do not transcribe the output into page markup, invent attribute reads as calls, or redraw it as separate before and after diagrams.
